steps.title: Cut and blanch the pork
steps.text: Cut the pork belly into chunky cubes about the size of a mahjong tile. Cover them with cold water and the ginger slices, bring to a boil and skim the foam, then drain and rinse the pork.

steps.title: Melt the sugar to amber
steps.text: Put the rock sugar in a dry wok over low heat and stir until it melts into a deep amber caramel. Add the pork and turn it until every piece is coated.
steps.quote: Watch the color. Tea color, honey color, stop. If it goes dark it is bitter and you start again.

steps.title: Wine, soy and the sweet spices
steps.text: Splash in the Shaoxing wine, then the light and dark soy sauce. Tuck in the knotted scallion and star anise and stir until the pork is shiny and red.

steps.title: Braise low and slow
steps.text: Pour in hot water until it just covers the pork and bring to a boil. Turn the heat to low, cover and braise about an hour, then let the pot cool and keep it covered overnight.

steps.title: Reheat and reduce the sauce
steps.text: The next morning, warm the pork gently, then take off the lid and turn up the heat. Spoon the sauce over the pork until it thickens into a glossy glaze.

steps.title: Plate and serve hot
steps.text: Spoon the pork and all the glaze onto a deep plate, scatter fresh scallion greens over the top and bring it to the table while it is still steaming.

memories.text: The first time she made this, she burned the sugar three times, and Grandpa ate it anyway.
She makes this dish when somebody is coming home.
